key_insight: ArogyaSutra combines a multilingual multimodal medical dataset with a multi-agent reasoning framework to improve medical question answering in English and seven Indic languages.
clinical_relevance: The work points toward more equitable AI support for patients and clinicians in low-resource Indian settings where medical questions and images are often shared in native languages.
method: Built ArogyaBodha, a large multilingual multimodal medical QA dataset from eight sources.
Covers 31 body systems, six imaging modalities, and 21 clinical domains across English plus seven Indian languages.
Introduced ArogyaSutra, an actor-critic multi-agent system with tool grounding, dual memory, and trajectory distillation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved multilingual medical reasoning accuracy across all Indic languages, with ablations supporting the role of each component.
watch_item: Performance is reported from abstract-level experiments, so real-world clinical reliability, bias, and safety in deployment still need careful validation.
paper_title: ArogyaSutra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Medical Reasoning in Indic Languages
